citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (2021). DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. WACV 2021.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad; Computer Vision Center, UAB)
description: DocVQA is a large-scale dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images, consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The dataset covers a wide variety of document types (letters, forms, reports, tables, etc.) and requires models to read and interpret text within the layout and structure of documents to answer natural language questions.
name: DocVQA
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 independent annotations per question (stage 1 and stage 2 workers each provide answers independently; a third review stage is applied when stage 1 and stage 2 answers do not match)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer mismatches between stage 1 and stage 2 were flagged for a third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt (due to language issues or ambiguity) were excluded from the dataset. Human performance was measured at 94.36% accuracy (ANLS 0.981) on the test split, serving as an upper bound.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web-based annotation tool (remote workers); annotation effort supported by Amazon
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages: (1) Workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, instructed to ask questions answerable from text in the image and to enter answers verbatim. Multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted. (2) A second worker was shown the image and questions (without stage-1 answers) and required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question; workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. (3) If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions/answers or ignore them.
rai:dataBiases: Documents are sourced exclusively from the UCSF Industry Documents Library covering only 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections because they have a good number of non-binarized images, introducing a collection bias. Most documents are from the 1960–2000 period. A large majority of questions start with "what is the", asking for date, title, total, amount or name, reflecting a question-type bias.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, downloaded from different collections across 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Pages were hand-picked from 6,071 industry documents spanning documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Binarized images were minimized; pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions and answers were collected via remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, organized under different industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) and collections. Documents include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text, spanning many decades and a wide variety of document types (letters, forms, reports, agendas, memos, scientific reports, transaction documents, tables, publications, financial reports, telephone records, contracts, articles, emails, graphics, notes, budgets, minutes, photographs, invoices).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Source documents span from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018; most documents are from the 1960–2000 period.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding the structure of the document is crucial. There is a large performance gap between existing models and human performance (94.36% accuracy). OCR errors can result in incorrect answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models struggle with questions based on figures, diagrams, photographs, and handwritten text. The dataset is limited to documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (5 industries).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality being a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application and serialized in top-left to bottom-right order. The dataset was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train (39,463 questions, 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions, 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions, 1,287 images) splits.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a "purpose-driven" approach in document image analysis and recognition research, enabling intelligent reading systems that can respond to ad-hoc information requests expressed in natural language. This could drive practical applications in document understanding and information extraction from real-world documents.
rai:dataUseCases: Visual Question Answering on document images; benchmarking document understanding models; driving "purpose-driven" document image analysis and recognition research; evaluating models that combine visual and textual cues for reading and interpreting document structure (tables, forms, figures, handwriting).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A commercial OCR application was used to extract OCR tokens from document images for use in baselines and upper bound computations.
